title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
hook: Tuning the sparsity penalty on an autoencoder is fiddly. Use a top-k constraint instead and you can dial sparsity directly — and scale SAEs to GPT-4.
key_points: Uses k-sparse (top-k) autoencoders to control sparsity directly, dropping the L1 penalty tuning.
Trained a 16-million-latent autoencoder on GPT-4 activations over 40 billion tokens.
Finds clean scaling laws relating reconstruction quality to autoencoder size and sparsity.
Introduces feature-quality metrics that improve as the autoencoder grows.
content_html: Leo Gao, Tom Dupré la Tour, Henk Tillman, and colleagues at OpenAI tackle a stubborn practical headache in dictionary learning: the L1 sparsity penalty is hard to tune and trades off cleanly against reconstruction in messy ways. Their fix is to use k-sparse (top-k) autoencoders that fix the number of active features directly, then scale the recipe up — training a 16-million-latent autoencoder on GPT-4 activations over 40 billion tokens.
extra_html:
How it works

Instead of penalizing activation magnitude with an L1 term and tuning its weight, a top-k autoencoder simply keeps the k largest latents and zeroes the rest, so sparsity is a knob you set, not a hyperparameter you hunt for. With that in hand, the team trains very large autoencoders and finds clean scaling laws: reconstruction quality improves predictably with autoencoder size and chosen sparsity. They also introduce feature-quality metrics that get better as the autoencoder grows, giving a way to judge progress beyond raw reconstruction loss.

Why it matters

This is OpenAI's take on sparse autoencoders, and it makes the method more of an engineering discipline than an art. Controlling sparsity directly removes a brittle tuning step, and the scaling laws suggest that bigger autoencoders keep buying cleaner features rather than hitting a wall. Together with Anthropic's work on Claude 3 Sonnet, it signals a shared push to make dictionary learning a reliable, scalable lens on frontier models.

related.hook: GPT-4 clears the bar on a wide range of professional and academic benchmarks - passing the bar exam near the top of the score range, for instance - while accepting both text and images as input.

related.hook: Before you train a giant sparse autoencoder, just look at the geometry. ICA Lens revives a classic method to surface interpretable directions in an LLM with no dictionary training at all.

related.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
related.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.
